newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-UK M4 growth to slow as repo distorts.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-UK M4 growth to slow as repo distorts.

text.p: M4, the broad measure of Britain's money supply growth, is forecast to have slowed in January but that may me be more to do with distortions from the gilt repo market than softer consumer spending.
A Reuter poll of economists found a consensus forecasting M4 growth of 1.0 percent in January, allowing the year-on-year rate to slow to 9.1 percent from 9.5 in December.
The figures will be released at 0930 GMT on Thursday.
The government has a monitoring range of three to nine percent, a band that the money supply measure has barely visited in the last 18 months.

A deceleration in broad money supply would be welcomed by the government, but the main reason for the apparent tail-off in money supply growth in January is technical -- the fledgling gilt repo market, just a year old.

"The annual growth rate of M4 is likely to ease because the upward distortion arising from the introduction of the repo market a year ago will, henceforth, fall out of the annual comparison," said David Philpotts, UK economist at Schroders.
He noted that December's M4 figure had been distorted downwards by a surprise downturn in repo activity. The broad money measure dropped 0.2 percent, the first monthly fall since 1992.

Most economists based their forecasts on a public sector debt repayment of about 3.5 billion stg. In fact, a massive 5.82 billion pounds was repayed in January, thanks to a flood of corporate tax and value added tax receipts.
That will have acted as a fiscal tightening and pushed money supply growth lower still.

"It is our belief that overseas investors were net buyers of the gilt market in January which, when combined with good domestic buying, implies that the public sector could have made a significant negative contribution to money supply growth," said Brian Hilliard, economist at Societe Generale Strauss.
For that reason, M4 growth would slow despite a bounceback in bank and building society lending to the tune of eight billion pounds, he said.

M4 bank and building society lending figures will be released alongside the money supply data on Thursday and are forecast to show a hefty 7.2 billion stg rise, according to the consensus, having dropped by 3.8 billion the month before.

Hilliard said the breakdown of the figures could hold the key clues as to the level of high street spending. "In particular, strong lending to the personal sector is more likely to boost domestic consumption than other forms of money supply growth."
But some economists see no scope for M4 growth to ease.
Michael Saunders, UK economist at Salomon Brothers, expects a hefty 10.2 percent year-on-year increase in M4 and said there was little sign of a slowing trend.
"Our forecast implies that over December and January together the average monthly gain was 0.8 percent, compared to an average monthly gain of 0.9 percent in the first 11 months of 1996," he said.
Monthly mortgage lending figures from the Building Societies Association will come out at the same time as the Bank of England unveils its M4 data.
Net new mortgage commitments worth 3.6 billion pounds are forecast to have been approved in January, just above December's 3.5 billion.
